properties.title: Segment tree crowns
properties.description: U-Net tree-crown segmenter: a ResNet-50 encoder taken from the DeepForest NEON_OAM detector, with a U-Net decoder trained on OAM chips of Freetown (the Guru trees dataset) and OSM tree labels (polygons, and tree points turned into crown discs). It predicts the tree canopy of each chip as a probability map and returns one polygon per canopy patch in EPSG:4326, holes included. Inference scales each chip to the model's resolution from the zoom and row in its OAM file name, then runs one ONNX pass; thresholding, polygon tracing and georeferencing run in the pinned ts-hot library. The base checkpoint is the trained U-Net (deepforest_UNet_OAM, layer4 of the encoder fine-tuned): pixel IoU 0.570 on the Guru validation chips and 0.404 on its test chips at threshold 0.3. The test score is lower mostly because many test chips carry no OSM labels although they show canopy; see the model card.
properties.mlm:name: deepforest-unet-tree
properties.mlm:architecture: U-Net (ResNet-50 encoder of DeepForest NEON_OAM, bilinear upsampling decoder)

providers.name: Weecology (DeepForest)

fair:metrics_spec.name: Pixel Precision
fair:metrics_spec.description: Share of predicted tree pixels that are tree in the labels, summed over the val split at the inference threshold. Labels: polygons, and tree points as crown discs; points without a diameter are ignored.

fair:metrics_spec.name: Pixel Recall
fair:metrics_spec.description: Share of labelled tree pixels that the model predicts as tree, summed over the val split at the inference threshold.

fair:metrics_spec.name: Pixel F1
fair:metrics_spec.description: Harmonic mean of pixel precision and recall over the val split.

fair:metrics_spec.name: Pixel IoU
fair:metrics_spec.description: Intersection over union of the tree class over the val split: intersecting pixels divided by the union of predicted and labelled tree pixels.

mlm:output.name: tree probability
mlm:output.description: ONNX output `probability`: per-pixel probability of tree canopy in model-input pixels, before thresholding.

mlm:output.name: tree canopy
mlm:output.description: Tree canopy polygons after thresholding, tracing, a minimum area and simplification, one polygon per feature, with holes.

label.description: Class name of the predicted class (tree).

confidence.description: Mean probability of the pixels of the polygon.

source.description: File name of the chip the polygon was detected in.

fair:split_spec.description: Spatial block split on OAM-x-y-z tile coords: chips grouped into (x // block_size, y // block_size) blocks, whole blocks assigned to train or val, because neighbouring chips share canopy and trees cut at chip borders. Chips must be named OAM-x-y-z.tif; any other name is rejected. Chips without a label are kept as background examples.

fair:hyperparameters_spec.description: Fine-tuning epochs. With epoch_fraction 0.1, ten epochs are one pass over the chips (the best Guru run). One epoch at epoch_fraction 0.1 took about 12 minutes on an RTX 4060 laptop GPU.

Chips per training batch. Each chip is scaled to the model's resolution (about 3x at zoom 20) before the network, so memory per chip is high (about 3.3 GB at batch 4 with layer4 training). Measured on the Guru chips (756 px): about 1.6 GB of GPU memory at batch 2 and 2.9 to 3.3 GB at batch 4; larger batches were not run.
AdamW learning rate of the decoder (the encoder stage that trains uses encoder_lr_factor times this). 3e-4 and 3e-3 scored the same on the Guru chips. Tried at 3e-4, 1e-3 and 3e-3.
AdamW weight decay.
Share of the chips held out as spatial validation.
Seed for the block order of the spatial split.
Side of a spatial block, in tile units.

Keep the ResNet-50 encoder frozen, except the stages from unfreeze_from on. BatchNorm statistics always stay frozen. With false the whole encoder trains (unfreeze_from and encoder_lr_factor then default to none and 1.0 in the code).

With a frozen encoder, still train the ResNet stages from this one on. layer4 was the one change that helped on the Guru chips (validation IoU 0.570 against 0.559 with the whole encoder frozen). layer3 and shallower stages were not tried.
Learning-rate multiplier for the encoder weights that train. 0.1 was better than 0.3 on the Guru chips.
Gradient clipping norm; 0 disables clipping.
cosine decays to 0 over all batches of the run; none keeps the learning rate constant.
Batches of linear learning-rate ramp-up.
Each epoch trains on a fresh random fraction of the chips. 0.1 gives a validation point every tenth of a pass; raise it for a small dataset.
Epochs without a better validation loss before training stops.
Weight of the Dice loss next to the binary cross-entropy; 0 uses cross-entropy only. 0, 0.5 and 1.0 scored within 0.002 IoU on the Guru chips. Tried at 0, 0.5 and 1.

Augmentation of the training chips: none, a random mirror, or a random quarter turn plus mirror (dihedral). None of the augmentations changed the Guru score by more than 0.003 IoU, so all are off by default.
Brightness and contrast jitter of up to 1 +/- this, and gamma exp(+/- this), on the training chips; 0 is off. Tried at 0.2.
Random rescale of the training chips and their masks by 1 +/- this; 0 is off. Tried at 0.15.
Chance that a training chip is blurred or JPEG-compressed, imitating coarser imagery; 0 is off. Tried at 0.3.
Probability from which a pixel is tree canopy. 0.3 is the best F1 on the Guru validation chips; 0.2 to 0.4 scored within 0.002 IoU.
Polygons smaller than this many model-input pixels are dropped (400 px is 1 m2 at 0.05 m). Swept from 0 to 1600.
Douglas-Peucker tolerance in model-input pixels; 0 keeps every pixel edge. Swept from 0 to 3.
Gaussian smoothing of the probability before the threshold; 0 is off. No gain on the Guru chips and 5 to 8 times slower decoding.
Radius of a square opening of the mask before tracing, which removes thin bridges and specks; 0 is off.
Radius of a square closing of the mask before tracing, which fills thin gaps; 0 is off.
Interior holes smaller than this many pixels are filled; 0 keeps every hole. Tried at 50 and 200.
Metres of ground per pixel the network sees. Training and inference must use the same value. A narrow band around the training scale; other values were not measured.
Cap on the longest side of a scaled chip, which bounds memory at coarse zooms.

checkpoint.title: deepforest_UNet_OAM: the trained U-Net (NEON_OAM ResNet-50 encoder with layer4 fine-tuned, decoder trained on the Guru trees chips). The starting point for fine-tuning
